title: ORDER_CANCELLED (v1)
description:
Published by Order Service to `ticketflow.orders.cancelled` when the customer gives up on an order. Consumed by the Payment Service, where it is the compensation trigger.

It is a separate topic from `orders.created` because the consumer reads it for the opposite reason: one starts a charge, the other undoes it. Sharing a topic would force the Payment Service to discriminate by type inside a single flow, and a routing mistake there means charging a cancelled order.

Two orderings are possible and both are normal:

  * cancellation reaches the Payment Service before it charged - nothing is charged
  * cancellation reaches it after - the money left, and the answer is a refund

Kafka orders within a partition, not across topics, so the consumer must handle both. The record key is the orderId, the same key used on `orders.created`.

`totalAmount` and `currency` travel in the event so the refunder knows how much to give back without asking anyone. Looking it up would be the synchronous service-to-service call this project does not allow.

reason.description: Why the order ended. Today always the customer's own request; the expiry job is a different status and does not publish this event.

totalAmount.description: The full order amount. The upper bound of what may need refunding - the Payment Service refunds what it actually captured, never more.

paymentMethod.description: Needed for the case where this event arrives before ORDER_CREATED: the Payment Service records an already-cancelled charge so it can never be made, and a charge - even a stillborn one - has to say by which method.
